thread.title: Next 50 Stocks: What Investors Should Watch for in May

title: Next 50 Stocks: What Investors Should Watch for in May
text:
David Marino-Nachison April 24, 2018 3:22 p.m. ET 
Here are 5 of the top confirmed May events for investors who follow stocks in the Barron’s Next 50 , with links to webcasts and other information when available. Newsletter Sign-up 
Days and times of these events may change, and this list may be updated periodically. Times below reflect the scheduled start time for management’s conference call with investors; financial results may be announced earlier via press release. 
Tuesday, May 1 
Apple (AAPL)— quarterly financial results, 5 p.m. ET . Wall Street is looking for quarterly EPS of $2.69, according to FactSet’s mean of 30 estimates. Apple watchers may look for information about upcoming changes to the iPhone lineup, though some analysts say pessimism about the X is overdone . 
Snap (SNAP)— quarterly financial results, 5 p.m. ET . Wall Street is looking for a quarterly loss of $0.28 per share, according to FactSet’s mean of 25 estimates. Its last report caused the shares to pop, but they have fallen to early 2018 levels since . 
Wednesday, May 2 
Tesla (TSLA)— quarterly financial results , 5:30 p.m. ET. Wall Street is looking for a quarterly loss of $3.53 per share, according to FactSet’s mean of 30 estimates. The company’s latest release of Model 3 production levels and targets hasn’t quieted questions about its need to secure additional funding, though the shares have recovered from early April lows. 
Tuesday, May 8 
Electronic Arts (EA)— quarterly financial results , 5 p.m. ET. Wall Street is looking for quarterly EPS of $1.16, according to FactSet’s mean of 26 estimates; the company has guided investors toward $1.14. Some investors have turned their attention to questions of whether “Battle Royale” games like Fortnite might dig into Electronic Arts’, and others’, business . 
Thursday, May 17 
Walmart (WMT)— quarterly financial results , 7 a.m. ET. Wall Street is looking for quarterly EPS of $1.12, according to FactSet’s mean of 30 estimates. Concerns about digital sales growth marked the response to the company’s last report, but the company’s pricing strategy has won it applause since.
